newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan fund stake to speed growth.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan fund stake to speed growth.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc will see faster growth in its investment management business with the planned purchase of a 45 percent stake in a major U.S. mutual fund company, analysts and industry sources said.
J.P. Morgan, which already has an in-house mutual fund capability, said Wednesday morning it will pay about $900 million for the stake in closely held American Century Cos.
A Wall Street analyst, who did not want to be identified, said the move is viewed positively because it also expands the company's presence in a higher-margin business.

"The general thought with J.P. Morgan is that it has too much dependence on lower-margin business with white shoe (blue chip) companies," said the analyst. "They need to take actions such as this, and probably more."
He said doing business with the largest corporate customers "does not always result in high profit margins" and J.P. Morgan is more exposed than the average bank to lower- margin businesses.
J.P. Morgan said it will form a business partnership with American Century to pursue growth opportunities in asset management and personal financial services.
An industry source said the American Century business in partnership with J.P. Morgan's existing business will be able to grow quickly.
In a news release, J.P. Morgan said the first initiative of the partnership will be to offer defined contribution pension plans to corporate plan sponsors.

The defined contribution retirement plan business is considered one of the fastest-growing areas in U.S. financial services. Analysts have said that the growth prospects were one of the reasons Morgan Stanley & Co Inc merged with Dean Witter Discover earlier this year.
The analyst who requested anonymity said J.P. Morgan telegraphed its move in advance.

At the annual meeting in May, chairman and chief executive Douglas Warner III said investment management was one of the areas J.P. Morgan was looking at for expansion. The company has been making similar statments to analysts for some time.
In midday trade, the company's shares were up 1-3/16 at 115-7/16.
